Any state-sector banking/payments IT buy therefore passes through DKÜ's framework agreements — making DKÜ a mandatory gatekeeper and an early indicator of state IT demand and of which vendors hold framework positions.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor /hirek/ and /kozerdeku-adatok/ for framework agreements and annual reports; monitor kozbeszerzes.dkuzrt.hu for DKÜ's own procurement procedures. The IDPR application (idpr.dkuzrt.hu) is credentialed and out of scope for collection.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on centralised state IT procurement
queries_used: Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség DKÜ központosított informatikai közbeszerzés dkuzrt.hu

candidates.source_name: KEF – Központosított Közbeszerzési Portál (kozbeszerzes.gov.hu)
candidates.why_relevant: The centralised public procurement system portal (keretmegállapodások / KM framework agreements) through which many state entities buy hardware and services, including terminals and IT equipment. KM numbers (e.g. KM08) appear directly in state contract documents, so the portal explains the contracting route behind many awards.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the framework-agreement (keretmegállapodás) listings; map KM identifiers to award documents found elsewhere.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from a NAV contract document referencing KM08
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Adatbázis kozbeszerzes.hu adatbázis szerződések kereső hirdetmény API

candidates.source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Beszerzések, pályázatok (procurement & tenders page)
candidates.why_relevant: Magyar Posta is a state-owned entity and a major payments actor (postal payment orders, cash handling, agent banking for a partner bank). Its own procurement page carries calls that are not always duplicated cleanly in the gazette, and reveals planned modernisation of postal payment and counter systems.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly page diff plus cross-check against EKR/TED notices where ajánlatkérő = Magyar Posta Zrt.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on Magyar Posta procurement
queries_used: Magyar Posta Zrt közbeszerzés pénzforgalmi szolgáltatás közbeszerzési eljárás

candidates.source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) – Közbeszerzés / közérdekű gazdálkodási adatok
candidates.why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority under the Kbt. Its procurements cover supervisory reporting systems, payment-system oversight tooling and cash infrastructure — a direct read on regulator-side system change. The published contract annexes also state MNB's standard IT contractual requirements.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the közbeszerzés page and the beszerzési eljárások section; archive the contractual annex documents as a baseline of MNB IT requirements.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on MNB as contracting authority
queries_used: MNB Magyar Nemzeti Bank közbeszerzési eljárások közzététel szerződések mnb.hu közbeszerzés

candidates.source_name: NISZ Nemzeti Infokommunikációs Szolgáltató Zrt. – Közbeszerzési információk & Közadat
candidates.why_relevant: NISZ operates the state's shared infocommunication infrastructure that public payment and e-government services run on. It publishes full annual közbeszerzési terv PDFs and the actual signed contracts (szerződések), giving unusually granular visibility into scope, price and delivery deadlines.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual/quarterly fetch of the közbeszerzési terv PDF (versioned with 'mod' suffixes — capture each modification) and enumeration of the szerződések PDF directory.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on state IT service provider procurement
queries_used: NISZ Nemzeti Infokommunikációs Szolgáltató Zrt közbeszerzés közérdekű adatok szerződések

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság (KDB) – decisions database
candidates.why_relevant: Remedy-procedure decisions expose contested requirements in banking/payments tenders — e.g. a D.677/2024 decision touching credit-institution IT system development reference criteria. These documents reveal specification detail, bidder identities and the real technical bar, and they flag procurements at risk of delay.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic keyword search ('hitelintézet', 'pénzforgalmi', 'bankkártya', 'terminál') over the decision database; download decision PDFs from the media/szinkron path.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search; PDF surfaced directly in seed-query results
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság határozatok kereső dontobizottsag.kozbeszerzes.hu

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – online services & databases hub
candidates.why_relevant: Single index page enumerating all official procurement databases and online services (notice search, contract database, KDB decisions, CPV code lists, registers). The most efficient snowball hub for discovering further authoritative endpoints in this cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off enumeration, then re-check semi-annually for new/retired services.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on the procurement database
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Adatbázis kozbeszerzes.hu adatbázis szerződések kereső hirdetmény API

candidates.source_name: Átlátszó (atlatszo.hu) – Közpénz investigative reporting on centralised IT procurement
candidates.why_relevant: Investigative outlet that reconstructs pricing and vendor patterns in DKÜ-routed state IT procurement (e.g. Aug 2024 piece on state bodies overpaying under centralised IT procurement). Useful as an interpretive/critical layer that surfaces contracts and anomalies not obvious from the raw notices.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/tag monitoring on 'közpénz' and 'DKÜ'; treat claims as leads requiring primary-document confirmation.
queries_used: Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség DKÜ központosított informatikai közbeszerzés dkuzrt.hu

candidates.source_name: NAV (Nemzeti Adó- és Vámhivatal) – közzétételi lista, megkötött szerződések
candidates.why_relevant: The tax authority is a large public buyer whose systems touch payment acceptance, online cash registers and e-invoicing/e-payment interfaces. Its published contract archive (organised by KM framework and year) gives concrete evidence of vendors and delivery deadlines in tax-side payment infrastructure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the kozadat contract directory tree (paths under /kozadat/altalanos_kozzeteteli_lista/3_3_mukodes/kozbeszerzes/) and index contract summaries by year and framework.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from a NAV contract PDF surfaced in a procurement-database search
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Adatbázis kozbeszerzes.hu adatbázis szerződések kereső hirdetmény API

candidates.why_relevant: Bilingual practitioner guide explaining EKR mechanics, registration, and the relationship between EKR, Közbeszerzési Értesítő and TED. Useful for correctly designing the collection method and understanding what is and is not publicly visible without registration.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off read for methodology; not for factual claims.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from EKR and TED searches

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for an MNB public-consultation register (társadalmi egyeztetés / véleményezés / ajánlástervezet). No general-purpose MNB consultation hub surfaced on mnb.hu; the only structured draft-publication surface found is aszp.mnb.hu/rendelettervezetek (reporting decrees only). Consultation on ajánlás drafts appears to run through password-protected channels with industry associations, and via ad-hoc 'szakmai konzultáció' news items.
negative_findings.result_summary: Consultation visibility on the MNB site is partial and event-driven, not a register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Forward-looking A3 signal (pre-publication drafts, comment deadlines) is structurally weaker for MNB soft law than for the EU authorities; the felügyeleti hírek feed and industry associations must compensate.

negative_findings.description: Reporting found that draft recommendations are made available to financial organisations for consultation via password-protected internet access through their interest-representation bodies (érdekképviseleti szervek).
negative_findings.result_summary: Draft-stage consultation material is behind credentialed access we should not attempt.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Do not plan any collection against gated MNB consultation areas; route this coverage through published outputs and association members instead.

negative_findings.description: Searched hu for 'szabályozási hírlevél' / 'felügyeleti hírlevél'. Only historical (2013-era) supervisory newsletters surfaced; no evidence of a current, regularly published MNB supervisory newsletter product.
negative_findings.result_summary: Assume no active MNB regulatory newsletter; rely on RSS /rss/11.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids building a collector against a discontinued channel.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetch-verified beyond three hub pages (felugyeleti-szabalyozo-eszkozok, /rss). All other URLs come from search-result metadata and are recorded with confidence scores, not liveness claims.
negative_findings.result_summary: Liveness must be established by the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents false 'verified' status propagating into the source registry.

negative_findings.description: Neither Nemzeti Jogszabálytár (njt.jog.gov.hu) nor magyarkozlony.hu documents a public API, bulk download, or open-data export. NJT's homepage lists search, topic filters, ABC lists and registration-based change monitoring, but no machine interface. Magyar Közlöny is distributed as digitally signed PDFs behind opaque hashed download paths.
negative_findings.result_summary: Collection must be built on HTML scraping of stable per-act URL patterns plus PDF text extraction; no official structured feed exists for either binding-text source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines the engineering shape and fragility of the whole A3 statutory pipeline for Hungary, and means URL-pattern drift is the main long-term breakage risk.

negative_findings.description: Searched in English for a Hungary-specific PSD3/PSR transposition plan, draft amendment to the Pft., or announced national deadline. All retrieved material was EU-level law-firm and vendor commentary on the EU timeline (plenary vote expected late May 2026, OJ publication mid-2026, PSR application ~21 months later, PSD3 transposition into 2027–2028).
negative_findings.result_summary: No Hungarian national PSD3 transposition instrument, draft, or announced deadline was found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: PSD3 is the largest pending payments obligation for HU PSPs; the absence of any national signal so far means the first detection will come from the Kormány törvényalkotási programja or a kormany.hu draft consultation, and those two must be monitored specifically for it.

negative_findings.description: Search results indicated that parlament.hu's advanced 'Irományok lekérdezése' query interface may require authentication, while the plain 'Folyamatban lévő törvényjavaslatok' listing and direct iromány PDF paths (parlament.hu/irom42/{n}/{n}.pdf) appear openly reachable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a hypothesis, not a verdict — no fetch was performed against the query form, so the gate is unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If the structured query form is gated, bill monitoring must rely on listing scraping plus predictable PDF paths, which is workable but less precise for filtering by subject.

negative_findings.description: net.jogtar.hu (Wolters Kluwer) and adt.arcanum.com are commercial platforms whose terms of service for systematic automated retrieval were not read in this pass, though both were reachable in search and net.jogtar.hu offers an open free tier.
negative_findings.result_summary: Reuse/scraping permissions for the two commercial consolidations remain unestablished.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The automated pipeline should be built on the state-run NJT (explicitly a free public service) and use commercial databases only for manual cross-checks, to avoid a ToS problem.

negative_findings.description: NJT advertises a translations section (/forditasok, /translations), but no evidence was found in this pass that consolidated Hungarian financial-sector statutes (Hpt., Pft., MNB payment decrees) are maintained in authoritative, up-to-date English.
negative_findings.result_summary: Binding-text coverage for this cell is effectively Hungarian-only; English material found was secondary commentary.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any downstream consumer working in English will depend on machine translation of the Hungarian binding text, with the accuracy risk that carries for dates and obligations.

negative_findings.description: Searches for Temenos, Backbase and Finastra press releases naming MBH Bank, Gránit Bank or K&H Hungary returned no vendor announcement of a Hungarian implementation; only generic vendor-comparison content and Wikipedia entries.
negative_findings.result_summary: No confirmed Temenos/Backbase/Finastra Hungarian bank reference found in this pass. MBH's core selection surfaced instead as Thought Machine.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents false attribution of Hungarian core-banking share to the best-known global vendors; the actual public trail points elsewhere.

negative_findings.description: No AML/KYC vendor press release (SAS, Napier, NetGuardians and similar) naming a Hungarian bank implementation was found, despite MNB having fined OTP and MBH for AML/CTF failures.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic AML-vendor listicles and regulator/law-firm content; no supplier-side reference for HU AML remediation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The strongest compliance-driven buying signal in Hungary (AML enforcement) currently has no visible supplier-side trace — a real blind spot for the indirect route, not merely a search failure.

negative_findings.description: Microsoft and IBM customer-story searches produced no Hungarian bank case study naming a regulatory driver; only general banking-guide content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hyperscaler reference coverage for HU banks confirmed only for Google Cloud/OTP in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests hyperscaler reference pages must be crawled directly on their own site search rather than via general web search.

negative_findings.description: No stable Hungarian-language term set was found for 'partner directory' / 'customer reference list' as used by vendors selling to banks; Hungarian vendors mix 'referencia', 'ügyfeleink', 'esettanulmány', 'PR' and sometimes have no such page at all.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian vendor sites are inconsistent in labelling reference material, making generic HU queries low-yield.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be actor-driven (enumerate vendors first, then crawl each site) rather than query-driven.

negative_findings.description: The Portfolio Financial IT 2025 sponsors page (/tamogatok) was surfaced by search but its sponsor list content was not retrieved in this pass; the page's existence is confirmed by the search result only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sponsor roster not yet extracted — treat as unverified, not absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the highest-value pointer in the cell; extraction should be prioritised in the collection phase.

negative_findings.description: No Hungary-specific job board or filter dedicated to regulatory/compliance roles in financial services was found; there is no HU equivalent of a 'regtech/compliance jobs' vertical board. All signal must be extracted by keyword filtering on general boards and employer career portals.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched hu and en for sector-specific HU compliance job portals; only general boards (profession.hu, CVOnline, Jobline, Jooble, Indeed) and employer/agency sites surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must be keyword-driven and multi-source rather than relying on a single vertical feed, raising noise and requiring a curated HU glossary.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language queries combining instant payments terminology with hiring ('állás azonnali fizetési rendszer AFR pénzforgalom projektvezető szabályozás bank') returned regulatory and market content (MNB rules, qvik/AFR 2.0 analysis) but no job advertisements.
negative_findings.result_summary: AFR/qvik hiring signal is not reachable via open web search; it sits behind board search forms and employer ATS listings that general search engines index poorly or late.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The instant-payments limb of this cell needs direct on-site searching of profession.hu, GIRO and bank career portals rather than search-engine discovery; treat absence of search hits as an indexing artefact, not absence of hiring.

negative_findings.description: Exact open-positions listing URLs for UniCredit Bank Hungary and JobsGarden were not pinned down; only section/landing pages were observed. UniCredit HU roles may be hosted on the UniCredit group ATS rather than the .hu domain.
negative_findings.result_summary: Landing pages identified (unicreditbank.hu/hu/rolunk/karrier..., jobsgarden.hu) but not the canonical vacancy list.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These entries need one resolution pass before automated monitoring; recorded as unverified rather than dead.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn Jobs, the richest source for English-titled Budapest hub roles and recruiter posts naming client regulatory programmes, is login-gated and its ToS prohibits scraping.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only public search-result stubs are visible without authentication.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A meaningful share of the cell's signal is only collectable manually or via a licensed data provider; budget human review time or accept a coverage gap.

negative_findings.description: No public Hungarian source was found that tracks consultancy engagement wins or programme staffing for banks (no HU equivalent of a public tender/consulting-mandate register covering private banks). Only the consultancies' own recruitment ads are visible.
negative_findings.result_summary: Big Four HU career pages found; no register of who is staffing which bank's regulatory programme.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Attribution from consultancy hiring to a specific institution's programme will remain inferential, not evidenced.

negative_findings.description: No single consolidated public calendar of Hungarian banking/payments regulatory events was found; MNB itself has no unified 'események' calendar covering supervision, payments and green finance together — event announcements are scattered across felügyeleti hírek, penzforgalom/konzultacio, penzugyi-stabilitas/konferenciak-eloadasok and greenfinance/esemenyek.
negative_findings.result_summary: Four separate MNB sub-sites must be polled instead of one calendar.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must treat MNB event discovery as a multi-endpoint crawl, otherwise consultations will be missed.

negative_findings.description: Searches for downloadable slide decks from MNB payments-themed professional days and from GIRO Zrt. professional days did not surface a public, systematic deck repository; decks appear only ad hoc, attached to individual news items.
negative_findings.result_summary: Slide-deck harvesting will be opportunistic rather than systematic for payments events.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Speaker slides are the highest-value artefact in this cell; their absence means agendas and speaker lists must carry the analytical load.

negative_findings.description: Several event URLs (ffs.ap.hu, digitalpayment.hu, iir-hungary.hu legacy query URLs, hunfintech.com) were seen only in search results and were not fetched in this pass; some are edition-specific and may rotate per year.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs recorded with moderate confidence; liveness left to the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Edition-scoped conference URLs commonly move (e.g. /2025/ → /2026/), so the collector needs a fallback to the organiser root domain.

negative_findings.description: Conference attendance and most training programmes (Portfolio, IIR, Bankárképző, Big-4 webinars) are paid or registration-gated; only agendas and speaker lists are consistently public.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public layer = agenda + speakers; content layer = gated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets a hard ceiling on what can be lawfully collected in this cell and argues for agenda/speaker-metadata collection rather than content capture.

negative_findings.description: A targeted English query naming the Budapest Business Journal returned no BBJ articles at all; results were law-firm guides and MNB pages instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: BBJ listed as a candidate on actor-map grounds only, with confidence lowered to 0.6 and no example article URLs. Its indexing/liveness is unverified, not disproven.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: BBJ is the presumed primary English channel for Hungarian bank-regulation news; if it is weakly indexed, English coverage of HU supervision depends more on vendor services (Vixio) and law-firm alerts than on local English press.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language queries about MNB fines and payment-rule consultations returned mostly mnb.hu press releases and net.jogtar.hu statute pages rather than press articles.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search engines rank the supervisor's own sajtokozlemenyek and the consolidated law database above trade press for these keywords.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For this press-focused cell it means discovery via generic keyword search is biased toward officialdom; press monitoring must be done via each outlet's own tag pages/RSS rather than via search engines.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian journalistic outlet was found that maintains a structured, machine-readable tracker of MNB supervisory fines or consultation deadlines.
negative_findings.result_summary: Coverage is article-by-article; the only list-like sources are MNB's own annual press-release indexes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any enforcement/deadline timeline must be assembled by the collector from unstructured articles cross-checked against MNB primary releases; no press shortcut exists.

negative_findings.description: No candidate URL in this slice was fetched; all entries rest on search-result evidence only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confidence scores reflect strength of search evidence, not reachability. Telex, Index, BBJ and Hungary Today are inference-based and carry no example article URLs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve these before any are promoted to the standing source register.

negative_findings.description: No RSS feed, open API, bulk export or documented result-URL pattern was found for the MNB decision search (hatarozatkereso.mnb.hu). The MNB landing page documents filters and numbering but not any machine interface.
negative_findings.result_summary: Collection will likely require HTML/XHR scraping of a JavaScript search form rather than a clean feed; ingestion cost and breakage risk are higher than for GVH or NAIH.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most important enforcement register in the cell; if it cannot be reliably automated, coverage of MNB sanctions degrades to press-release monitoring, which omits smaller and non-publicised decisions.

negative_findings.description: PBT (Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület) publishes only its binding decisions and recommendations, anonymised and with a short summary — not the full case file, and not settlements-by-agreement in detail.
negative_findings.result_summary: The public PBT register is a partial, redacted view of the complaint landscape; the quantitative picture must come from the annual reports rather than from counting published items.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Under-counting complaint volumes or mis-reading dispute mix would distort the 'issues before they become rules' early-warning function this cell exists to serve.

negative_findings.description: Neither the NAIH decision register nor the BHGY court-decision collection offers a financial-sector or NACE-style filter; both must be mined by keyword.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank/PSP-relevant items must be isolated with a Hungarian keyword list (bank, hitelintézet, pénzforgalmi szolgáltató, bankkártya, követeléskezelő, fizetési megbízás), accepting recall/precision trade-offs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword-only retrieval will miss cases where the controller or litigant is named without sector wording, so enforcement counts from these sources are lower bounds.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, consolidated Hungarian register of court challenges against MNB supervisory decisions (i.e. outcomes of közigazgatási per against felügyeleti bírság) was found as a standalone product; such rulings are dispersed inside BHGY/Kúria and must be reconstructed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in Hungarian for the anonymised-decision collections; found general-purpose portals only, no MNB-specific litigation tracker.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Whether sanctions survive judicial review is the strongest evidence of how durable a supervisory position is; without a tracker this must be assembled case by case.

negative_findings.description: Several useful commentary/aggregation layers are commercial: Wolters Kluwer Jogtár, Vixio Regulatory Intelligence, and partially Portfolio and Adózóna.
negative_findings.result_summary: These offer better-structured enforcement digests than free sources but require subscriptions; free primary registers remain sufficient for the core record.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Budget decision: subscribing buys speed and structure, not unique primary facts.

negative_findings.description: Only one URL in this slice was fetched directly (the MNB decision-search landing page). All other URLs come from search-result metadata and are recorded as unverified pending the deterministic liveness pass. One slug in particular (otthonapenzugyekben.hu …/panaszkezelas/) is transcribed from a search result and may be misspelled or moved.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs supplied with confidence scores, not liveness claims.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents downstream treatment of scouted URLs as verified endpoints.

negative_findings.description: Searched in English for a Hungary-specific regulatory horizon-scanning tracker or compliance-deadline product.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic global RegTech vendors surfaced (Vixio, FinregE, Regulativ, Kodex AI, Mitti listicles). None demonstrated Hungary-specific coverage in public material; the search engine itself noted no HU-tailored tracking systems in results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is no off-the-shelf HU deadline tracker to lean on: the deadline dimension must be assembled from MNB's adatszolgáltatási naptár, Magyar Közlöny hatálybalépés dates, and EUR-Lex application dates.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for a dedicated Magyar Bankszövetség regulatory-monitoring newsletter ('szabályozási figyelő hírlevél', 'jogszabályfigyelés').
negative_findings.result_summary: No public, subscribable regulatory newsletter endpoint was found for the Banking Association; only news, press-release and working-group listing pages plus legacy quarterly PDF reports.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The association's regulatory positioning is likely circulated to members only, so its influence on drafts must be inferred from press releases and working-group pages rather than captured directly.

negative_findings.description: The acronym 'MNB' is noisy in Hungarian search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries for 'MNB archívum' returned Magyar Nemzeti Levéltár (MNL, national archives), penzvero.hu (mint) newsletters, and a third-party 'MNB Archívum' news-tag aggregator (rsshirek.hu/tag/mnb) rather than the central bank.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated HU query expansion must anchor on 'Magyar Nemzeti Bank' or site:mnb.hu, otherwise the collector will ingest archives-of-the-nation and coin-mint content as central-bank material.

negative_findings.description: No liveness verification was attempted for most URLs in this slice; only https://www.mnb.hu/rss was actually fetched this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: The feed index at mnb.hu/rss returned a parseable list of 11 named feeds. All other URLs are recorded from search results and are unverified pending the deterministic liveness pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Per playbook, unfetched or failed URLs are hypotheses; the verification pass must resolve them and distinguish bot-defence (403) from relocation (404). njt.hu in particular exposes four parallel hosts (njt.hu, njt.jog.gov.hu, uj.njt.hu, or-archiv.njt.hu) that need canonicalisation.

negative_findings.description: Looked for an explicit MNB public-consultation ('konzultációs dokumentum' / 'vitaanyag') portal analogous to EBA/EU 'Have your say'.
negative_findings.result_summary: No dedicated MNB consultation portal surfaced in this run; MNB soft-law appears to be published as finished instruments under felugyeleti-szabalyozo-eszkozok rather than through an indexed consultation stage.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If MNB has no open consultation register, pre-decisional intelligence on HU supervisory expectations has to come from kormany.hu társadalmi egyeztetés, Bankszövetség working groups, and EU-level consultations instead.

negative_findings.description: Neither the hu-language search on kormany.hu consultation terms combined with 'pénzügyi szolgáltatások' nor the open-consultation listing on egyeztetes.kormany.hu surfaced any currently open banking or payments consultation. The only ongoing item observed on the portal was a road-safety dialogue (deadline 2026-09-09); the recently closed items were asset-recovery, secret-service archives and school-start support.
negative_findings.result_summary: No live HU banking/payments ministry consultation observed at scouting time; this is a point-in-time observation, not evidence that the channel is unused.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's channel must be monitored continuously rather than sampled — comment windows are short (5 working days internally, ~8 days publicly) and a sector draft can open and close between polls.

negative_findings.description: The egyeztetes.kormany.hu consultation portal page carried no visible RSS feed or documented API; the current kormany.hu generation likewise did not expose an RSS index in search results, although the frozen 2010-2014 and 2015-2019 generations both published /rss channel lists including one for the document archive.
negative_findings.result_summary: Machine-readable subscription for HU government consultations is unconfirmed on the current site; polling with diffing is the fallback.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Drives the collection architecture and cost for the whole A3 executive-branch channel, and creates a risk of missing short-window drafts.

negative_findings.description: The ministry-filtered dokumentumtár URL for Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium draft laws rendered 'Nincs találat' when fetched as static HTML, despite search-engine evidence of ~130 items under that filter with 2026 dates and April 2026 comment deadlines.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as a client-side-rendering hypothesis, not as a dead or empty source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector built on plain HTTP fetching would silently record zero HU ministry drafts — a false-negative failure mode that must be guarded with a non-zero-results assertion.

negative_findings.description: https://kormany.hu/kormanyzat/nemzetgazdasagi-miniszterium returned HTTP 404; only the frozen 2020-2025 generation page for NGM could be reached in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Current-generation NGM ministry landing URL unresolved; recorded as unverified/moved rather than dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ministry slugs and site generations change with each government cycle, so hardcoded ministry URLs will rot; resolution must go through the Kormányzat index each run.

negative_findings.description: The run scope names both Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium and Pénzügyminisztérium. Evidence in this pass shows NGM as the current owner of financial/economic legislation and NGM-issued ministerial instructions dated 2024, while older financial-sector decrees carry the historic NGM/PM/NFGM prefixes. No page was found that authoritatively maps the PM to NGM portfolio transfer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ministry-name lineage (NFGM → NGM → PM → NGM) partially inferred from decree prefixes rather than from a confirmed source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical backfill and decree-prefix parsing will mis-attribute drafts unless the ministry lineage is explicitly resolved.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching returned almost nothing on the HU executive branch's own consultation channel; the only substantive English-language route into HU pre-adoption drafts found was the EU TRIS notification database.
negative_findings.result_summary: English is not a viable primary monitoring language for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms Hungarian-language collection and parsing (including Hungarian PDF extraction) is mandatory infrastructure for A3, not optional.

negative_findings.description: Nem találtam olyan MNB-oldalt vagy hivatalos magyar nyilvántartást, amely egyetlen, gépileg olvasható táblázatban vezetné az EU-instrumentumok magyar alkalmazási/átültetési státuszát és határidőit (EU act → magyar norma → hatálybalépés).
negative_findings.result_summary: Az információ szét van szórva: MNB felügyeleti hírek, ajánlások, njt.hu, Magyar Közlöny, EUR-Lex NIM. A státusz-összerakást a gyűjtőnek kell elvégeznie.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A cella lényege a határidőkövetés; egységes forrás hiányában saját crosswalk-táblát kell építeni, különben a határidő-riasztás megbízhatatlan.

negative_findings.description: A PSD3/PSR-re nem találtam stabil, bevett magyar rövidítést vagy hivatalos magyar munkacímet a magyar szabályozói kommunikációban; a szakirodalom az angol 'PSD3'/'PSR' rövidítést használja a 'harmadik pénzforgalmi irányelv' és a 'fizetési szolgáltatásokról szóló rendelet' körülírással.
negative_findings.result_summary: Magyar keresés PSD3-ra döntően angol rövidítéssel indexelt találatokat ad; nincs MNB-oldali dedikált PSD3 hub.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A tisztán magyar kulcsszavas monitorozás elmulasztaná a PSD3-tartalmat; a lekérdezéseknek vegyes hu/en terminológiát kell használniuk.

negative_findings.description: Nem sikerült megerősítenem egy dedikált, nyilvános MNB 'megfelelési nyilatkozat' (comply-or-explain) gyűjtőoldal létezését az EBA/ESA iránymutatásokhoz; a magyar státusz csak az EBA/ESMA saját compliance table PDF-jeiben látszik.
negative_findings.result_summary: A célzott hu keresés MNB-oldali gyűjtőt nem hozott, csak EU-oldali compliance table-öket.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A magyar megfelelési státuszt EU-forrásból kell kinyerni, ami nyelvi és formátumbeli többletmunkát jelent (PDF-táblák Hungary-sorainak parse-olása).

negative_findings.description: A jelen körben nem végeztem oldal-lekérést (fetch) egyetlen jelölt URL-en sem; minden URL a keresési eredményekből vagy kanonikus intézményi gyökerekből származik.
negative_findings.result_summary: Minden URL ellenőrizetlen (unverified) — élőségüket a determinisztikus verifikációs lépésnek kell megállapítania.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Az mnb.hu mély URL-jei hosszúak és átszervezésre hajlamosak; egy 404 valószínűbben áthelyezést jelent, mint megszűnést.

negative_findings.description: No publicly accessible Hungarian-market Visa or Mastercard rulebook, bulletin, or mandatory-deadline register was found. Searches in Hungarian ('szabálykönyv', 'kötelező határidő', 'bankkártya elfogadás') returned only consumer marketing, FAQ and media pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Card scheme rulebooks and Announcement/Bulletin releases appear to be member-only (licensed) documents with no HU-specific public portal identified in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A whole mandatory-deadline stream (scheme release cycles, mandates on issuers/acquirers) is invisible from open sources; the workstream must rely on proxies (acquirer merchant manuals, PSP release notes, trade press) or licensed access.

negative_findings.description: GIRO's participant-facing portal online.giro.hu/dokumentumtar was surfaced by search but its public accessibility was not established in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a hypothesis: likely partially or fully gated behind a participant login. Not confirmed dead or blocked.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If gated, the richest technical change-notice channel is unavailable, and monitoring must fall back to the public giro.hu/dokumentumok mirror with a lag.

negative_findings.description: No RSS/Atom or structured change-log feed was identified for GIRO Zrt. rulebook amendments; changes appear to be signalled only by new dated PDF filenames.
negative_findings.result_summary: Detection will require filename/hash diffing rather than feed subscription.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Increases collection cost and raises the risk of missing a short-notice effective date.

negative_findings.description: No public, versioned 'qvik szabálykönyv' (qvik scheme rulebook) document with an explicit version number and change history was located; MNB publishes FAQ pages, an arculati kézikönyv and a technikai kézikönyv instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: The qvik scheme obligation set appears distributed across MNB recommendations, technical/brand manuals and the BKR ÜSZ annexes rather than a single rulebook.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deadline extraction for qvik must aggregate several document families; a single-document monitor would under-cover.

negative_findings.description: No downloadable CSV/XLSX/API export of the MNB Intézménykereső result sets was identified from the pages inspected; the portal appears to be a form-driven HTML search with 'SpecialData?name=...' list endpoints for niche lists only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk extraction of the full HU licensed-institution population may require HTML parsing of paginated results, or falling back to the EBA PSD2 register export and the ECB MFI download for the PI/EMI and credit-institution slices respectively.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines pipeline design and cost for the core actor-enumeration step; an undetected export would waste scraping effort, and an assumed export that does not exist would break the pipeline.

negative_findings.description: A dedicated, separately published list of payment-institution AGENTS (pénzforgalmi közvetítők / PSD2 agents) was not located as its own page; agent data appears to live inside the Intézménykereső intermediary tabs (Hpt./Bit. based), which are oriented to money-market and insurance intermediaries.
negative_findings.result_summary: PSD2 agent enumeration for Hungary may be more reliably obtained from the EBA central register's agent records than from a HU-only page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell explicitly targets agent registers; mis-locating them would leave the distribution layer of the payments market unmapped.

negative_findings.description: MNB MiCA/CASP licensing guidance was found, and secondary Hungarian media assert several exchanges now hold MNB authorisation, but no official MNB-published list of licensed kriptoeszköz-szolgáltatók was located at a stable URL in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: CASP enumeration currently rests on Intézménykereső queries and the ESMA MiCA register rather than a dedicated MNB list page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Crypto-asset service providers are a new regulated population directly adjacent to payments; missing the authoritative list risks relying on media claims, which must not be treated as register facts.

negative_findings.description: The exact boundary between free and fee-based company-register access (e-cegjegyzek.hu / Céginformációs Szolgálat) was not pinned down; free 'online céginformáció' exists but full extracts and bulk/XML supply appear to be chargeable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as partly_paid with legal collection routed through the Céginformációs Szolgálat's adatszolgáltatás rather than scraping.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bulk scraping a fee-based statutory register would be a legal and contractual risk; the access terms must be read before any pipeline is built.

negative_findings.description: All URLs in this slice were obtained from search results and, for four of them, from successful content fetches; the remainder were not individually fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: No URL here is claimed as verified-live; a deterministic liveness pass should confirm. Any 403/timeout should be read as bot-defence, not as a dead source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents false 'dead source' verdicts on bot-defended government portals such as alk.mnb.hu and e-cegjegyzek.hu.

negative_findings.description: No standalone, clearly-labelled Pillar 3 / 'nyilvánosságra hozatal a kockázatkezelésről és a tőkemegfelelésről' landing page was located in this pass for K&H Bank Zrt., Erste Bank Hungary Zrt., UniCredit Bank Hungary Zrt., Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. or Gránit Bank Nyrt. Only CIB and legacy MKB/MBH Pillar 3 documents surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in hu using the exact statutory phrasing returned CIB, MKB and MNB guidance only; the other five banks' equivalents were not surfaced by search-engine results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pillar 3 reports are the annual anchor for capital/supervision signals; missing them for five of seven target banks leaves the capital-adequacy dimension of this cell under-covered.

negative_findings.description: No RSS/Atom or JSON feed was found for any of the seven banks' hirdetmény pages; all change notices appear to be HTML listings plus PDFs.
negative_findings.result_summary: Every discovered notice board (OTP, K&H, Erste, UniCredit, Raiffeisen, MBH, Gránit) is a rendered page or a document repository, several behind JS-driven frontends (e.g. gate.erstebank.hu documentId GUIDs).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be scrape-and-diff rather than feed-subscribe, raising fragility and cost, and making the archive pages (K&H, UniCredit, Raiffeisen) disproportionately valuable.

negative_findings.description: No bank-issued customer notice explicitly tied to the 2026 Hungarian payment-fraud/qvik regulatory package was found from OTP, K&H or the other target banks; only MNB press releases and press coverage surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: The hu query combining bank names with qvik / azonnali fizetés / 2026 jogszabályváltozás returned MNB, Portfolio and fintech.hu items, not bank hirdetmények.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core thesis is that hirdetmények are the earliest precise evidence of a rule biting; if such notices exist they are likely inside PDFs not indexed by search engines, implying collection must crawl the boards directly rather than rely on search discovery.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetched or liveness-checked; all entries are search-derived. The Erste gate.erstebank.hu documentId links in particular are opaque GUIDs of unknown persistence.
negative_findings.result_summary: Discovery ran on web search only in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification must treat any 403/timeout on these hosts as bot-defence rather than death, and must re-derive Erste document links from the hub page each run.

negative_findings.description: The referenced routine playbook path (C:/Users/User/Dropbox/.../source_discovery_scout/routine_prompt.md) is a Windows path not present on this macOS host, so the full method document could not be read.
negative_findings.result_summary: Method followed from the inline instructions only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any cell-specific conventions defined only in the on-disk playbook were not applied.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for a standalone payments/e-money/card-acquiring industry association ('Magyar Pénzforgalmi Szolgáltatók', 'pénzforgalmi szolgáltatók egyesülete', 'Magyar Elektronikuspénz szövetség', 'Bankkártya Szövetség'). No such body appeared in results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Results returned only the supervisor (MNB payment-institution pages), the State Treasury, commercial bank product pages and an unrelated auditors' association (MPGE). No dedicated Hungarian payments-provider association was surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If no separate payments association exists, payments-regulation lobbying in Hungary is likely channelled through the Banking Association's payments working group and the Fintech Association's TPP working group — which changes where to look for consultation responses on payment rules.

negative_findings.description: Looked for a current national savings-cooperative federation (Országos Takarékszövetkezeti Szövetség / takarékszövetkezetek szövetsége) as a distinct association.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only a historical reference found: the savings-cooperative federation was a Banking Association member from 2008 to 2018. No live standalone federation site was surfaced, consistent with the sector's consolidation into the integrated/MBH structure.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means cooperative-bank interests may no longer have an independent association voice in Hungarian consultations; do not assume such a body exists and do not fabricate a URL for it.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for a debt-collection industry association ('Magyar Követeléskezelők' / követeléskezelők szövetsége).
negative_findings.result_summary: No formal association site surfaced; results were generic debt-collection directories and unrelated pages. The Banking Association does, however, run a standing working group on enforcement, receivables management and insolvency.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Receivables-management regulation is an active Hungarian file; if there is no dedicated association, the Banking Association working group and PVOE are the substitute sources to monitor.

negative_findings.description: Attempted to locate a structured archive of Magyar Bankszövetség consultation responses / position papers on specific draft laws (a 'véleményezések' or 'állásfoglalások' repository).
negative_findings.result_summary: The site nav exposes Kiadványok (Kommunikék, Publikációk, Jelentések, Hitelintézeti szemle) and Sajtóközlemények, but no separate consultation-response repository was observed. Positions appear embedded in press releases and quarterly reports.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must extract positions from prose in press releases and quarterly report PDFs rather than from a clean per-consultation index; budget for text mining rather than structured harvesting.

negative_findings.description: Magyar Fintech Szövetség membership and some outputs run through an external Typeform (form.typeform.com/to/yAI25bSk); the annual Fintech Report may sit behind a download form.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public site exposes nav, board composition and a members page; deeper member-only material (e.g. the regulatory white paper) was not publicly located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The most substantive fintech-side regulatory positions may be member-gated; plan for press-coverage proxies rather than direct collection, and do not submit forms on the user's behalf.

negative_findings.description: Searched for 'Blockchain Koalíció' and 'Magyar Kriptoszövetség' as named Hungarian crypto self-regulatory bodies.
negative_findings.result_summary: Neither name resolved to an organisation. Crypto-regulation advocacy in the results is attributed instead to the Magyar Fintech Szövetség's legal working group and to individual firms (Revolut, eToro, CoinCash) plus advisory firms (PwC) and community sites.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Crypto/MiCA-adjacent lobbying in Hungary appears firm-led and fintech-association-led rather than run by a dedicated crypto association; these speculative names must be recorded as not-found, not as sources.

negative_findings.description: No EY Hungary financial-services regulatory newsletter or alert hub was located, in either Hungarian or English, despite targeted queries combining 'EY Magyarország', 'pénzügyi szolgáltatások' and 'szabályozási'. Deloitte, KPMG and PwC all yielded identifiable Hungarian publication hubs; EY did not.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only an IFLR1000 directory profile for EY Law Hungary was found; no publication or newsletter URL.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Leaves one of the four audit firms uncovered in a cell whose premise is that Big Four alerts date and translate obligations early. EY's content may be behind a subscription/registration wall or on a global insights path not surfaced by these queries.

negative_findings.description: Queries naming Szecskay, Forgó Damjanovic, VJT & Partners, Dentons Budapest and Bird & Bird Budapest alongside Hungarian terms for newsletter, financial regulation and payment services returned only firm homepages, team pages and directory listings — no dated financial-regulatory alert feeds.
negative_findings.result_summary: Firms confirmed to exist and be active in Hungary, but no evidence found of a financial-regulation alert channel at any of them in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are plausible interpreters whose alerts, if they exist, are not indexed against Hungarian financial-regulation vocabulary. They should be checked by direct site visit (news/hírek paths) rather than by search engine in the next pass.

negative_findings.description: The Deloitte Hungary legal content appears to span two site trees (www2.deloitte.com/hu/hu/pages/jog/... and www.deloitte.com/hu/hu/services/legal/...), with equivalent banking/finance pages on both. The www2 paths may be a legacy tree in the process of retirement.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both URL families were returned as live search results in the same pass; neither was fetched, so neither is confirmed or dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector pinned to only the www2 newsletter hub risks silently going stale if Deloitte completes the migration. Both trees should be monitored until one demonstrably redirects.

negative_findings.description: No RSS/Atom feed URL was visible on the KPMG Hungary blog landing page when fetched, despite the site behaving like a standard blog platform.
negative_findings.result_summary: Feed absent from the rendered page; a conventional /feed/ endpoint was not tested.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether collection can be feed-based (cheap, reliable dates) or must be HTML-diff based (heavier, date extraction less reliable). Should be probed deterministically in the verification pass.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian professional-body or association-run regulatory alert bulletin for the interpreter layer (e.g. a Magyar Ügyvédi Kamara or Magyar Bankszövetség compliance circular aimed at translating MNB deadlines) surfaced in this cell's searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on Hungarian bar/banking-association terms did not return an interpreter-style bulletin within this pass's query budget.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Association circulars, where they exist, are often the earliest bilingual restatement of an obligation and would be a high-value addition; absence here is a search gap, not evidence the channel does not exist.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, publicly documented REST/JSON API was found for the Hungarian Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (KBA) or for EKR. Searches surfaced only web search interfaces, saved-search e-mail alerts and PDF issues.
negative_findings.result_summary: Machine-readable national-level access appears to be limited to TED (for above-threshold notices) and third-party re-publishers such as Opentender; national below-threshold data likely requires HTML scraping or PDF parsing of the Közbeszerzési Értesítő.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for this cell must budget for scraping/PDF extraction rather than assuming an official API; this affects reliability and maintenance cost of the pipeline.

negative_findings.description: Searching in Hungarian for Magyar Posta public procurement procedures specifically for pénzforgalmi (payment) services returned mainly the company's ÁSZF/terms and fee announcements, not procurement notices.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only a generic 'Beszerzések, pályázatok' landing page was identified; no payment-systems-specific Magyar Posta tender was located in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Magyar Posta's status as an in-scope contracting entity for payment-related buys is asserted by the cell rationale but not yet evidenced with a concrete notice; needs targeted confirmation via EKR/TED buyer search before relying on it.

negative_findings.description: No page fetches were performed in this pass; all candidates come from search-engine result metadata and snippets. No URL in this slice should be treated as liveness-verified.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs are recorded with confidence scores only; EKR in particular is a JavaScript/session-heavy portal likely to resist simple fetching.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve every URL; a failure on ekr.gov.hu should be treated as a bot-defence hypothesis, not as a dead source.

negative_findings.description: GIRO Zrt. (operator of the Hungarian interbank clearing system, MNB-owned) was hypothesised as a public-sector-adjacent buyer of payment infrastructure, but no procurement-publication route for it was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: No GIRO procurement page or notice was found; whether GIRO qualifies as a contracting entity under the Kbt. remains unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: GIRO procurements would be among the highest-value payment-infrastructure signals in Hungary; a confirmed publication route would materially strengthen this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: The decisions-and-rulings search (határozatok és végzések keresése) is a form-driven application; no static index or documented API was identified, so bulk historical harvesting of supervisory findings and fines is unproven.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe the search page's network calls for a JSON endpoint; if none, budget a headless-browser paging collector keyed on date range and sector.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage of pre-publication drafts is limited to reporting decrees (aszp rendelettervezetek). Draft ajánlások and vezetői körlevelek have no observed public draft register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add industry associations (Magyar Bankszövetség, and any payments/fintech association) as a companion cell — they receive drafts and often comment publicly.

coverage_gaps.description: Effective dates (hatálybalépés) and submission deadlines live inside PDF bodies and per-year reporting tables, not in listing metadata, so link-diffing alone will not yield a deadline calendar.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a HU-language PDF extraction rule set for 'hatályba lép', 'alkalmazandó', 'legkésőbb', '… munkanapig', 'tárgyhónapot követő'.

coverage_gaps.description: MNB emits instruments across at least four hosts/trees: www.mnb.hu/felugyelet, www.mnb.hu/penzforgalom, aszp.mnb.hu, zoldpenzugyek.mnb.hu, plus the legacy /archivum CMS. A single-tree crawler will silently under-collect.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define the MNB collection target as a multi-host set with per-host crawl rules; assert coverage by cross-checking each new felügyeleti-hír against the host trees.

coverage_gaps.description: MNB states recommendations are available in Hungarian; the EN mirror is partial and lags. English-only monitoring would miss most instruments and nearly all effective dates.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat HU as the system of record; use EN only for terminology reconciliation and cross-checks.

coverage_gaps.description: Several statutes that clearly belong in the watchlist were identified by name but not resolved to a specific NJT act ID in this pass: Pmt. (AML/CFT act), the consumer-credit act (Fhtv./Hitel tv.), the deposit-insurance provisions (OBA), and the ministerial decrees on fizetési számla váltás and on the pénzforgalmi szolgáltatók adatszolgáltatása.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a targeted NJT keyword pass ('pénzmosás', 'fogyasztónak nyújtott hitel', 'betétbiztosítás', 'fizetési számla váltás') to pin exact act IDs and add them to the diffing watchlist.

coverage_gaps.description: The current Hungarian ministry responsible for financial-sector rule-making (Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium / earlier Pénzügyminisztérium) was only reached indirectly through kormany.hu Dokumentumtár filters; its own decree and consultation pages, and the current tarsadalmiegyeztetes@ mailbox domain, were not confirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map the current ministry's own site section for jogszabálytervezetek, confirm the ministry filter ID on kormany.hu/dokumentumtar, and verify the live consultation mailbox.

coverage_gaps.description: NJT offers registration-based change monitoring and bookmarks, but whether those produce an email or RSS feed usable for automated alerting was not established; no RSS/Atom feed was identified on magyarkozlony.hu either.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Create an NJT account and test the változásfigyelés feature end to end; probe magyarkozlony.hu and mnb.hu for undocumented RSS endpoints before committing to pure polling.

coverage_gaps.description: Alkotmánybíróság and Kúria decisions can strike down or reinterpret binding financial-sector provisions and thereby move or void deadlines, but no source for those was scouted in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add alkotmanybirosag.hu and kuria-birosag.hu (plus their Magyar Közlöny-published AB határozatok) as a follow-up scouting target, or confirm they belong to a different coverage cell.

coverage_gaps.description: EUR-Lex NIM was identified as the EU-to-HU transposition bridge, but the specific CELEX list of directives in scope for HU banks and PSPs (CRD, PSD2/PSD3, CCD2, AMLD, DORA-adjacent, IFD) was not compiled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the in-scope CELEX watchlist and wire each to its EUR-Lex NIM tab filtered to Hungary, so a missing HU notification past a transposition date raises an alert automatically.

coverage_gaps.description: Card/ATM/self-service and cash-handling suppliers to Hungarian banks (e.g. Euronet, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Atleos, Printec-type integrators, Cardnet) were not systematically searched for Hungarian bank references in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over ATM/self-service vendor newsrooms and Hungarian-language 'bankjegykiadó automata', 'önkiszolgáló bankfiók', 'ATM üzemeltetés' queries.

coverage_gaps.description: Formal partner directories (Microsoft Partner Center, AWS/Google partner finders, Temenos/Oracle partner locators, IVSZ Hungarian ICT association member list) were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate partner-directory endpoints and filter by country=Hungary + financial services competency; IVSZ member list as the Hungarian-language anchor.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign-owned Hungarian subsidiaries (Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, K&H/KBC, CIB/Intesa) were not covered on the group-level vendor-announcement axis, where the parent group's supplier press releases may name the Hungarian unit.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search vendor newsrooms for parent-group names plus 'Hungary'/'Hungarian subsidiary'; also crawl group procurement/supplier portals.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian-language searching was performed on all main themes, but no Hungarian-language query was run against vendor newsroom domains directly (site-scoped HU queries).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run site-scoped Hungarian queries against identified vendor and integrator domains (4ig.hu, dorsum.eu, integra.hu, mindspire.hu, cardnet.hu) using 'referencia', 'esettanulmány', 'bevezetés', 'sajtóközlemény'.

coverage_gaps.description: Archived/older vendor reference pages and delisted case studies were not sought; vendors routinely remove references when contracts end.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan a Wayback Machine sweep of identified vendor reference and partner pages to recover removed Hungarian bank references and build a time series.

coverage_gaps.description: Smaller and specialist HU institutions were not covered: Gránit Bank, Magnet Bank, savings/credit cooperatives, Takarék-successor entities, Revolut Hungary (branch/licensed entity), Barion, OTP Mobil (Simple), and card/ATM processors — all subject to the same DORA/AML/instant-payments deadlines.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an actor list from the MNB institution register, then resolve a career-page URL per institution and add to the weekly watchlist.

coverage_gaps.description: Technology and outsourcing vendors serving HU banks (core-banking, payments, AML/transaction-monitoring, regulatory-reporting software and their local integrators) were not enumerated. Their HU job ads name the client-side deadline drivers as clearly as bank ads do.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate vendors from MNB DORA ICT-third-party registry context and HU banking-IT trade press, then monitor their HU career pages and profession.hu advertiser pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Organisational-change signals other than job ads (new directorates, executive appointments, internal reorganisations announced in press releases, cégjegyzék/company-register officer changes) were not scouted in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add HU company-register (e-cegjegyzek/Opten/Bisnode) officer-change monitoring and bank press-release feeds as a complementary weak-signal channel.

coverage_gaps.description: Job ads expire and are removed, so no historical baseline exists unless snapshots start now; several sources also lack visible posting dates in listing views.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Begin weekly snapshotting immediately with full ad text and first-seen/last-seen timestamps; consider archive.org submission for high-value ads.

coverage_gaps.description: The HU glossary used here is a first pass; terms not yet exercised include 'IKT-kockázatkezelés', 'digitális működési reziliencia', 'pénzmosás megelőzése', 'ügyfél-átvilágítás', 'belső ellenőrzés', 'kockázati kontroll', 'jelentésszolgálat', 'MNB ERA', 'STR/gyanús tranzakció bejelentés'.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Expand the query set with these terms across profession.hu, CVOnline and Jooble; measure hit rate per term and prune noisy ones (e.g. bare 'compliance', which also matches tax/ESG roles).

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage is Budapest-centric; regional boards (pecsallas.hu, egerallas.hu and similar) carry banking ads for branch and back-office locations outside the capital and were only glimpsed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Sample two or three regional boards for a quarter to test whether they carry any regulatory-programme roles; drop if noise dominates.

coverage_gaps.description: Sectoral regulators/bodies beyond MNB that host regulatory events were not covered in this pass: Ministry for National Economy (NGM) consultations, Hungarian Competition Authority (GVH) financial-sector workshops, NAIH (data protection) financial webinars, and the Budapest Stock Exchange (BÉT) academy.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up scout on ngm.gov.hu, gvh.hu, naih.hu and bet.hu event/consultation pages with Hungarian event terms.

coverage_gaps.description: Speaker rosters and slide decks increasingly live on LinkedIn and YouTube (event recordings, post-event recaps by MNB staff and law firms) rather than on organiser websites; this channel was not explored.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted pass over LinkedIn event pages/company posts and YouTube channels of MNB, Portfolio, FinTechZone and Bankárképző; note LinkedIn scraping restrictions and prefer manual/API-compliant access.

coverage_gaps.description: Law-firm client seminars and webinars (e.g. Hungarian banking/fintech practices) — a classic early-warning channel for imminent obligations — were not systematically enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout Hungarian financial-regulatory law firm event/insight pages with terms 'szeminárium', 'ügyfél tájékoztató', 'reggeli', 'webinárium'.

coverage_gaps.description: Archive depth was not assessed: it is unclear how far back each organiser keeps past agendas and speaker lists, which limits trend analysis on how topics migrate year to year.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each priority organiser, probe past-edition URL patterns and register Wayback Machine snapshots as a fallback archive.

coverage_gaps.description: Some organisers publish an English mirror (Portfolio /en/events) but most Hungarian training catalogues are Hungarian-only; English-only monitoring would miss the majority of the cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Make Hungarian-language crawling mandatory for this cell; use English mirrors only for cross-checking speaker affiliations.

coverage_gaps.description: No Hungarian-language legal/compliance trade press (e.g. Jogaszvilag, Ars Boni, Wolters Kluwer Jogtar newsletters) was searched or confirmed in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run hu queries such as 'jogaszvilag penzforgalom MNB rendelet', 'jogi szaklap bankjog valtozas hatarido' and evaluate legal trade press as a deadline/consultation early-warning layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Industry-association and vendor commentary channels (Magyar Bankszovetseg communications, GIRO/AFR operator briefings, card-scheme and PSP blogs) were not covered here, though press reporting frequently originates from them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a snowball pass on Bankszovetseg and GIRO announcements and identify which journalists/outlets consistently pick them up.

coverage_gaps.description: Portfolio, VG and hvg carry significant paywalled depth; Vixio is subscription-gated. Free tiers give headline+date but often not the operative deadline detail.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide on a subscription budget for Portfolio (highest value) and evaluate Vixio; otherwise treat press as a dating/pointer layer and take substance from MNB primary documents.

coverage_gaps.description: No archive strategy identified for retrieving pre-2020 Hungarian press coverage of supervisory actions; outlet tag pages are shallow and paginate unpredictably.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test outlet sitemaps and web.archive.org captures for Portfolio /bank and hvg MNB tag to establish historical depth.

coverage_gaps.description: No mapping yet of the specific Hungarian journalists who own the MNB-supervision and payments beats; bylines are the most reliable filter for high-signal coverage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest bylines from confirmed Portfolio /bank and hvg MNB-tag articles and build an author watchlist (including their public social accounts).

coverage_gaps.description: No source found yet for enforcement/complaint activity at the payment-scheme and infrastructure layer (GIRO Zrt. / instant payment system AFR incident and dispute handling, card scheme arbitration outcomes in HU).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted hu searches on 'azonnali fizetési rendszer AFR incidens', 'GIRO Zrt. üzemzavar', 'kártyatársasági chargeback vitarendezés' and check MNB payment-system oversight (felvigyázás) publications.

coverage_gaps.description: Payment fraud and authorised push payment (APP) dispute/liability enforcement was not separately scouted; the emerging PSR/PSD3 reimbursement debate will make this the dominant complaint category.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search hu for 'csalás áldozata visszatérítés bank MNB állásfoglalás', 'jóvá nem hagyott fizetési művelet visszatérítés', and en for 'Hungary APP fraud reimbursement supervisory expectation'.

coverage_gaps.description: Pointer sources for aggregated EU-level enforcement touching HU banks/PSPs (EBA breach-of-Union-law and peer-review outputs, EDPB one-stop-shop decisions, CJEU preliminary rulings originating from Hungarian courts) were identified only indirectly via the C-630/23 reference.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add EBA, EDPB and CURIA case-law search as standing pointer sources filtered on Hungary and on financial/payment subject matter.

coverage_gaps.description: The historical depth of hatarozatkereso.mnb.hu, the PBT recommendation register and the NAIH pre-GDPR archive was not established, so multi-year trend feasibility is unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: During the first collection run, probe the earliest retrievable date in each register and record it as a dataset property.

coverage_gaps.description: English coverage of Hungarian enforcement is thin and selective: MNB English pages exist for supervision and investor warnings, and sanctioned institutions occasionally publish English decision translations, but neither GVH decisions, NAIH decisions, PBT recommendations nor BHGY court rulings are systematically available in English.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for machine translation of Hungarian primary text as a pipeline stage rather than relying on English-language sourcing; keep hu originals as the authoritative record.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed machine-readable feed for Hungarian legislative output itself — Magyar Közlöny and njt.hu were not confirmed to expose RSS/API endpoints in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe magyarkozlony.hu and njt.hu for RSS, sitemap.xml, or JSON endpoints; if absent, build a dated-issue-list poller and a statute time-state differ.

coverage_gaps.description: SZTFH (Szabályozott Tevékenységek Felügyeleti Hatósága) was referenced only indirectly (crypto-oversight role, via a law-firm summary); its own publication/archive endpoints were not scouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated HU query set on 'SZTFH közlemények / határozatok / RSS' and add its document archive as a candidate; it is a second HU financial-adjacent supervisor besides MNB.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level consultation and deadline aggregators scoped to HU relevance (Commission 'Have your say', EBA/ESMA/EIOPA consultation registers and their RSS) were identified only conceptually; no concrete feed URLs were captured this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Capture the concrete RSS/ATOM endpoints for ec.europa.eu 'Have your say', EBA consultations, ESMA consultations, and add them as pointer candidates with HU-relevance filters.

coverage_gaps.description: EUR-Lex national implementing measures (NIM) for Hungary — the structured record of whether and when HU transposed a given directive — were not directly enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a NIM query against EUR-Lex (or CELLAR SPARQL) filtered to Hungary and financial-services directives to derive a transposition-deadline tracker.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian professional/practitioner aggregators beyond KPMG (e.g. ado.hu, jogaszvilag.hu, arsboni, Deloitte/PwC/EY HU alerts, jogtar.hu / Wolters Kluwer commercial legal databases) were not systematically scouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Second pass with HU queries on 'jogi hírlevél pénzügyi intézmények', 'jogtár előfizetés', 'adó.hu pénzügyi szabályozás' to fill the commentary/interpretation layer.

coverage_gaps.description: The MNB Adatszolgáltatói Portál calendar (aszp.mnb.hu) and the STEFI/ERA systems mix public calendar pages with authenticated submission systems; the public/private boundary is unclear.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Determine which aszp.mnb.hu pages are anonymously reachable and whether the calendar is backed by a JSON API; do not attempt access to ERA/STEFI authenticated areas.

coverage_gaps.description: The exact working query-parameter form and category-id semantics of the kormany.hu dokumentumtár filter (categories=2 = jogszabálytervezetek? ministry=10 = NGM?) were not confirmed; two different parameter conventions appeared in search results.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Drive the dokumentumtár with a headless browser once, capture the XHR/API calls it makes, and build the collector on that underlying endpoint rather than on the rendered HTML.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian law requires the responsible minister to publish a summary of received comments and a list of commenters, but no live example of such a summary page for a financial-sector draft was located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search specifically for the standard cover-sheet phrasing 'A társadalmi egyeztetés formájának' and for 'összefoglaló a beérkezett véleményekről' scoped to kormany.hu, and map where these outcome documents live.

coverage_gaps.description: The consultation portal lists 16 ministries. Beyond NGM and a glance at the Justice Ministry, other ministries that can originate banking/payments-adjacent rules (Miniszterelnökség, Igazságügyi Minisztérium for civil/consumer-credit law, Belügyminisztérium for AML/data) were not individually scouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate all ministry filter values on egyeztetes.kormany.hu and kormany.hu dokumentumtár and register each as a monitored channel with topic keyword filters rather than pre-selecting ministries.

coverage_gaps.description: Signals that precede even the consultation stage — Kormányinfó briefings, kormányülés agendas, and the government's own féléves jogalkotási program beyond the one autumn-2026 annex found — are only partially covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and register the full series of the Kormány féléves törvényalkotási/jogalkotási programja and the Kormányinfó transcripts as a standing forward-calendar feed.

coverage_gaps.description: robots.txt and terms of use were not inspected for kormany.hu, parlament.hu, torvenyfigyelo.hu or bankszovetseg.hu.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a compliance pass over robots.txt/ToS for every registered domain before enabling scheduled collection, and set polite crawl rates.

coverage_gaps.description: Most URLs recorded here come from search results or single fetches; liveness, stability and content-match have not been independently confirmed, and two fetches (ministry landing page, filtered dokumentumtár) failed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness/verification pass over all candidate URLs, treating 403/timeout as bot-defence and 404 as moved-needs-rediscovery.

coverage_gaps.description: Nem térképeztem fel a hazai AI Act intézményi réteget a pénzügyi szektoron kívül (piacfelügyeleti hatóságként kijelölt gazdaságfejlesztési miniszteri szervezet, Nemzeti Akkreditáló Hatóság, NAIH), pedig a bankokra vonatkozó nagy kockázatú MI-rendszerek kettős felügyelet alá eshetnek.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Külön felderítés a 2025. évi LXXV. törvény által kijelölt hatóságok saját közlemény-csatornáira, magyar keresőkifejezésekkel (MI-rendelet, piacfelügyeleti hatóság, bejelentő hatóság).

coverage_gaps.description: Az ECB/SSM és az euroövezeti fizetési infrastruktúra (TIPS, ECB payments) magyar relevanciájú csatornáit nem dolgoztam ki, pedig az azonnali euró átutalás 2027-es hazai elérhetősége ehhez kötődik.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Külön alcella: ECB payments/TIPS közlemények + MNB fizetési rendszer jelentés keresztolvasása, hu és en kulcsszavakkal (azonnali euró átutalás, TIPS csatlakozás).

coverage_gaps.description: Nem azonosítottam gépi hozzáférési utat (RSS/API) az MNB felügyeleti hírfolyamhoz és az ajánlás-jegyzékhez; jelenleg csak HTML-crawl feltételezhető.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Célzott technikai felderítés: RSS/Atom végpontok, sitemap.xml, és az mnb.hu oldalstruktúra stabilitásának tesztelése a gyűjtő megtervezése előtt.

coverage_gaps.description: A parlamenti szakasz (Országgyűlés irományok, bizottsági viták) mint az átültetés legkorábbi hivatalos jelzése nincs lefedve; a MiCA validálási kötelezettség eltörlése például parlamenti szavazás volt.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Adja hozzá a parlament.hu irománykeresőt mint direct forrást, watchlist-tel a pénzügyi tárgyú törvényjavaslatokra.

coverage_gaps.description: Card scheme layer (Visa CEMEA, Mastercard Europe) has no identified authoritative HU-facing source; only proxies and media.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Evaluate licensed access (Visa Online / Mastercard Connect via a partner institution) or systematically collect HU acquirer and PSP merchant manuals and release notes as proxies.

coverage_gaps.description: Domestic ATM/card processing and switching operators (e.g. processors serving HU banks) and the BÉT (Budapest Stock Exchange) trading-side rulebooks were not explored in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up sweep on 'kártyaelfogadói hálózat üzemeltető', 'ATM üzemeltető', 'BÉT szabályzat módosítás' to complete the infrastructure actor map.

coverage_gaps.description: Most confirmed effective dates found are 2024-2025; no 2026 forward calendar of Hungarian scheme deadlines was assembled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a deadline register by extracting hatálybalépés dates from KELER Hírcenter, giro.hu dated PDFs and MNB qvik pages, and reconcile against the EU IPR/VoP milestone calendar.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Hungarian scheme rulebooks is thin — GIRO publishes some EN business terms but Hungarian is the authoritative version.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Hungarian documents as primary and budget for HU-language parsing/translation; do not rely on EN mirrors for deadline extraction.

coverage_gaps.description: Registers for the non-bank consumer-lending and financial-enterprise segment (pénzügyi vállalkozás), and for independent ATM operators, were not separately mapped in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run Intézménykereső advanced search by institution activity type to enumerate 'pénzügyi vállalkozás' entries, and search hu terms 'ATM üzemeltető engedély' / 'készpénzkifizetés bankjegykiadó automata'.

coverage_gaps.description: No machine-readable API/open-data endpoint for HU registers was identified (e.g. an MNB open-data or data.gov.hu dataset mirroring the licensed-institution list).
